visual.pregunta: Your school has recently started a Culture Club. You have recently joined it and want to share your experience with the rest of the school. Write a text for the school magazine explaining what the club is, describing one session and encouraging other students to join. (450–600 words)
visual.floja:
Culture Club

The Culture Club is a club in my school. It is on Wednesdays. I am going to explain it.

In the club people talk about subcultures. There are goths, skaters and gamers. It is very interesting. One day a girl talked about goths. She showed photos and music. It was good and people liked it.

I think the club is good because people know other people and there are less stereotypes. It is important to be respectful.

You should join the club because it is very fun. It is in the library.

Thank you.
visual.porque: About 11/30: no byline, no hook or subheadings, nothing developed, and it ends with “Thank you”.
puntos: C: catchy title + subtitle, author, publication and date
C: hook paragraph with a rhetorical question to the reader
C: subheadings and paragraphs; more formal than a blog, still personal
C: no comments or hashtags (that would be a blog)
B (explaining): what the club is, when, where, who, its rule
B (describing): one session in detail – Marta’s presentation
B (encouraging): direct invitation, practical details, answer to the main doubt
B: decisive conclusion – “not a luxury; it is a necessity”
A: purposeful idioms – judge a book by its cover, pulled it off
A: worksheet vocabulary – stereotypes, self-expression, fit in
A: complex structures – relative clauses, passive, “It would be easy to…”

filas: appeal to the reader, rhetorical questions

visual.mal: Thanks for reading! Drop a comment below #school
visual.bien: That is a blog ending. An article ends with a decisive conclusion and a call to action: “Come and see for yourself.”

pregunta.q: “CAP” refers to Content, Audience, and Purpose.
Articles can include up to three images to support their content.
“Write to the director of the youth centre, whose name you do not know, asking for a room for your band.” How should you close?
opciones: Yours faithfully
Yours sincerely
Love
#bandlife

ideas: Catchy title on top, decisive ending
